sections.html:
Malden is a dense city in Middlesex County, just north of Boston across the Mystic River. About 66,263 people lived on its 5.1 square miles in 2020, roughly 13,000 per square mile. Neighbors are Melrose to the north, Medford to the west, Everett to the south, Revere to the east and Saugus to the northeast.

2020 housing measureMalden
Households26,024
Housing units27,721, with 6.1% vacant
Owner occupied47.2% of units
Median age35.7 years

Fewer than half of Malden homes are owner occupied, so renting is common. If you own a house with tenants, tell the buyer up front.

Malden grew around squares at its crossroads, and many neighborhoods take the name of the square at their center.

  • Squares: Malden Square at Main and Pleasant Streets, Converse Square, Oak Grove Square at the Oak Grove station, Bellrock Square, Judson Square, Maplewood Square and Linden Square.
  • Neighborhoods: Faulkner, West End, Edgeworth, Linden, Ferryway, Forestdale, Maplewood, Bellrock and Belmont Hill.
  • Landmarks by area: Bell Rock Memorial Park and the New England Coffee headquarters in Bellrock, Macdonald Stadium in Edgeworth, and Pine Banks Park shared with Melrose.

Maplewood got its name in 1847, when the president of the Saugus Branch Railroad bought 200 acres and planned wide streets with ornamental maples. Edgeworth was once the site of the Converse Rubber Factory, the original home of the Converse sneaker.

Puritans settled Malden in 1640, the town was incorporated in 1649, and it became a city in 1882. It once included Melrose, which separated in 1850, and Everett, which separated in 1870. The first mayor funded the Converse Memorial Library, built in 1885.

That long history means older housing. A house built a century or more ago can come with original layouts, older heating systems and decades of deferred work, and buyers who use a mortgage will see those items in their own inspection. A cash buyer prices them directly.

Malden is on the MBTA Orange Line, with stops at Malden Center and Oak Grove, and Malden Center is also a commuter rail stop. The city covers only about five square miles, so many streets are a short walk, bus ride or drive from a station.

  • U.S. Route 1 is the one limited access route through the city, linking Boston and the North Shore.
  • Routes 28, 60 and 99 run through as arterial roads.
  • Route 16 and Interstate 93 are a short distance outside the city line.
  • MBTA buses reach every adjacent community.

The Northern Strand Trail, also called the Bike to the Sea trail, gives a paved route from the Mystic River in Everett to Western Avenue in Lynn. Houses within walking distance of a station draw commuters, which helps a listing, but a cash buyer prices a house on its condition and numbers either way.

Malden has about 30 park sites, and open space is a selling point for houses near them. Fifty-six acres of the Middlesex Fells Reservation lie inside the city, Fellsmere Pond covers 25 acres, and the ArtLine, a series of murals and sculptures, runs along the Northern Strand Trail.

The Massachusetts Department of Fire Services requires a certificate of compliance from the local fire department showing that your smoke and carbon monoxide alarms meet the standard for a sale or transfer.

The state's steps are practical. Find out when your home was built and when the last building permit was issued, since the alarm requirements depend on those dates. List every alarm and check its manufacture date, because an alarm with no date has expired. Then call the fire department when you have a closing date. The department charges a fee for the inspection and certificate.

The deed excise under Chapter 64D, Section 1, is two dollars for each five hundred dollars of the sale price, or fraction of it, outside Barnstable County. Massachusetts keeps deeds in county registries, and most properties are recorded land. Ask the City of Malden's building and assessing offices about permits and bills tied to your address, and ask your attorney who pays the excise under your contract.

Tell the buyer about leases and rents at the start. Under the contract you can negotiate whether the house closes occupied or vacant, and a Massachusetts attorney can advise you on tenant notice rules. Many Malden sellers own a two or three family house with a mix of long-term and short-term tenants, so gather lease copies, rent records and any security deposit details before you ask for offers.

In a cash sale the buyer does not need a mortgage, so the timeline depends on the title work and on when you want to close.

  1. Tell the buyer about the house, any tenants and your timeline.
  2. The buyer reviews the property and presents a written offer.
  3. Once you accept, a Massachusetts attorney handles title and the purchase and sale agreement.
  4. Smoke and CO certification and any payoffs are arranged.
  5. The deed is recorded and you receive the proceeds.

Listing the same house means preparing it, showing it and waiting on a buyer's loan. Selling for cash trades a possible higher price for speed and certainty. For a Malden multifamily with tenants or an estate house full of belongings, that trade is worth thinking through.

After you accept an offer, the attorney orders a title search. It lists mortgages, liens and unpaid taxes or water charges, and each gets a payoff letter or a release. The fire inspection is booked, and the deed is drafted for the registry in Middlesex County. At the table you sign the deed and the settlement statement, your lenders and any back taxes are paid from the proceeds, and you keep what is left.

With no bank involved, the usual causes of delay are an old lien nobody remembered and an alarm inspection booked too late. In an older two or three family with several floors, a hard-wired alarm that fails can mean calling an electrician, so book the visit early enough to fix it.

sections.h2: What to bring to the table
sections.html: Pull together the latest tax bill, any water balance, a mortgage payoff statement and receipts for big repairs. With an inherited house, add the documents showing who may sign. A buyer who sees these early can give a firmer offer and a shorter timeline, and your attorney can finish the title review without waiting on missing pages.

faqs.q: How many people live in Malden, MA?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 66,263 residents in Malden, in 26,024 households. About 47.2 percent of housing units were owner occupied.

faqs.q: Is the Orange Line close to most Malden homes?
faqs.a: Malden has two stations, Malden Center and Oak Grove, and the city covers only about five square miles. Many streets are a short walk, bus ride or drive from one of them.

faqs.q: Do I need a certificate for smoke and CO alarms in Malden?
faqs.a: Yes. A certificate of compliance from the local fire department is needed when you sell or transfer a home. Call the Malden fire department for its fee and scheduling.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Malden two family with tenants?
faqs.a: Yes. Tell the buyer about the leases and rents at the start. You can negotiate whether the house closes occupied or vacant, and a Massachusetts attorney can advise you on tenant notice rules.

faqs.q: What does the Massachusetts deed excise tax cost?
faqs.a: It is two dollars per five hundred dollars of the price or fraction of it. Your contract and attorney will confirm who pays it.
